title: Rehearse the interview on a voice call. Then read your feedback.
lede: An AI interviewer that has read the same posting and your analysis asks you questions out loud. You answer by speaking, from your computer or your phone. It's practice, just for you: nobody else hears it, and nobody will contact you.
intro: The app's screens, as they are: the room during the call, and your feedback after it.

controls.voiceNote: The interviewer's voice is the one that interviews you in {{brand}} when you choose English.

lines.l1: Hi Guillermo, thanks for joining. I'll be interviewing you for the Full Stack Developer role at Orilla Software. We have about 12 minutes. To start, tell me briefly about your background and what drew you to this role.
lines.l2: Seven years of web apps. Today I run an ordering app for 120 restaurants, in React and Node.js. I want a product to grow with.
lines.l3: This role uses PostgreSQL or MySQL. Which database do you use, and for what?
lines.l4: PostgreSQL. I designed the payments tables and I write their migrations.
lines.l5: The team deploys on AWS. Have you used any cloud?
lines.l6: Not AWS. We deploy to our own server; I automated the deploys.
lines.l7: Tell me about a time your change broke production. What did you do?
lines.l8: A tip bug charged twice for an hour. I rolled it back, refunded everyone and told the team.

screens.label: App screen
screens.note: A replica of the app's screens, playing the example conversation. The app keeps the transcript with its times; it doesn't record the audio of your call.

gaps.r3: You named the database and what you do with it. Add it to your CV: it's what R3 is missing.
gaps.r5: You were clear about what you haven't done, and you showed something close. You didn't say how you'd learn it.

answers.a1: You answered with what you did in the database, not with a list of tools.
answers.a2: You said what happened and how you fixed it, but not what you changed so it doesn't happen again.

categories.communicationSkills: You answered in short, direct sentences and named what you did, not the tools around it.
categories.technicalKnowledge: PostgreSQL came with real work behind it: the payments tables and their migrations. AWS stayed at what you haven't done.
categories.problemSolving: On the tip bug you rolled back, refunded and told the team, in that order. Say what you changed afterwards.
categories.culturalFit: You said what draws you to the role, a product to grow with, and owned the production bug without blaming anyone.
categories.confidenceAndClarity: Direct about the gaps, with no filler. Some answers end on the task instead of the result.

worked.w1: Asked about the database, you answered with what you did, not with a list of tools.
worked.w2: On AWS you were direct instead of dodging the question.

workOn.o1: When you talk about the production bug, say what you changed afterwards so it doesn't happen again.
workOn.o2: End long answers with the result, not the task.

example.final: You answered with concrete facts and were direct about what you haven't done. The next step is to end every answer with its result: what changed afterwards.
